- [2011/03/11] Japan experienced a devastating earthquake and tsunami, claiming over 18,000 lives.
- [2016] Kumamoto prefecture in Japan was hit by a magnitude 7.0 earthquake, causing significant damage and claiming dozens of lives.
- [2018] A series of typhoons hit Japan, causing flooding and landslides, resulting in the deaths of over 200 people.
- [2019] Typhoon Hagibis hit central and eastern Japan, causing widespread flooding and landslides, but with a lower death toll due to improved disaster response systems.
- Japan has implemented a nationwide early warning system for earthquakes and tsunamis, capable of detecting an earthquake within seconds.
- Japan has improved evacuation plans, ensuring clearly marked routes, safe shelters, and conducting emergency drills.
- Japan has strict building codes focused on structural integrity and stability to withstand natural disasters, improved since 2011.
- Japan has enhanced communication during disasters using social media, TV broadcasts, and other media channels for real-time updates.
- Japan has improved coordination between government agencies like the police, military, and disaster management for efficient resource deployment.
- Japan's disaster response improvements have been a long-term process involving new laws, government agencies, and investments in infrastructure and equipment.
